$comment: Schematic reference-pose geometry in reach units, on the depth axis between two facing fighters (Phase J, Decision 0012 slice item 5). This is the 2D stand-in for authored animation clips: collision_model declares hitboxes attached to gloves with move_active_frames as their life, and animation_model fixes transforms to authored pose per tick - but no clips exist yet, so the fist's travel is authored HERE as a per-move extension profile, sampled per tick, swept as an interval, live only during active ticks. Consumed by the C++ core and its analyzer, deliberately NOT by the Python reference simulator, whose 1D model resolves contact through the staged pipeline's draws - that scoping is stated rather than implied, and Unreal's 3D authoritative implementation replaces this file's schematic when real clips land (Decision 0002). Every number is a tuning hypothesis.

body.half_depth_note: Twice this equals movement_model separation.min_center_distance_ru (0.28) on purpose: two bodies touch exactly when the separation clamp engages, so the movement model and the collision geometry describe the same pair of bodies rather than two that never meet.

guard.authoring_margin_note: Decision 0020 (gate G6). No posture extent may sit within this margin of plane_interception_min_extent unless a knife edge is explicitly intended and explicitly tested. Two lanes were authored exactly on 0.60 and were therefore decided by the first point of arm damage, or by whichever way a rounding landed: philly_shell body moved to the exposed side and active_hands head to the protected side. The margin is canon rather than a convention so it can be widened once and checked everywhere - tests/test_guard_threshold_margin.py enforces it for every posture and lane; the canon validator remains an implementation obligation in Issue #9.
guard.plane_note: The guard is a plane sitting plane_offset_ru in front of the body surface. It intercepts an incoming sweep in a height class only when the posture's authored extent for the volume covering that class reaches plane_interception_min_extent - so with high_guard's extents (guard_high 0.95, guard_body 0.55), the head lane is closed and the body lane is open, and 'body shots pay off against a high guard' falls out of the posture data and one threshold rather than being written anywhere as a rule (the core combat design rule, and Rule 4's counterplay against passive high blocking).

fist.profile_note: Extension interpolates linearly from retracted_ru to extended_ru over startup+active ticks (animation_model's per-move tick counts), so the fist is still travelling during its active window and the active-tick sweep is a genuinely moving interval. The hitbox is live only during active ticks (collision_model hitboxes.active_source = move_active_frames): startup is telegraph, not threat. Extensions sit just under each move's authored range band ceiling plus body reach, so a mid-band punch reaches through the mid band and whiffs beyond it - Rule 12's range gate expressed as geometry instead of a comparison.

height_note: Height stays a discrete class (collision_model's height_class vocabulary), not a coordinate: what is real in this schematic is the depth sweep. Numeric heights arrive with actual clips. blockable_either (the hook) maps to 'high' here as a NAMED SIMPLIFICATION: a hook travelling around a guard needs the lateral dimension this depth-axis schematic does not carry, so for now the hook meets the high plane like a straight. The around-the-guard path arrives with 2D geometry, and this mapping is where to look when hooks stop behaving like jabs. Note what the low mapping already gives away honestly: uppercut_rear is blockable_low in the move table, so against a high guard it comes up UNDER the closed head lane through the open body lane to the jaw - the classic guard-splitter, emergent from the same one threshold.
invariants: The fist sweep is evaluated against the defender's position at the evaluation tick, so footwork during an opponent's startup genuinely changes what the active window meets.
A guard plane never protects a height class whose covering volume the posture holds below the interception threshold - lanes are opened by structure, not by rule.
